ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, authorised representatives, material transaction counterparties, and any proposed bank signatories must be screened before incorporation against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU financial sanctions, HKSAR financial sanctions, and the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list. PEP checks must cover politically exposed persons resident in or connected to mainland China or Hong Kong, including family members and close associates of senior officials. Enhanced due diligence applies to state-owned enterprise shareholders, senior government officials, and pharmaceutical or healthcare counterparties classified as medium-risk. Continuous adverse-media, negative-news, asset-freeze, and secondary-sanctions checks are mandatory before any capital contribution or wire disbursement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and local Administration for Market Regulation Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of the WFOE must be registered in simplified Chinese characters comprising a four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and company type indicator (limited company). The Chinese name must be transliterated from the shareholder's lawful name where applicable; no traditional Chinese characters, Pinyin-only names, or English-only registration are permitted. The English name is optional, cannot be the statutory name, and must not duplicate any existing SAMR-registered name. For heparin sodium anticoagulant manufacturing, the industry component must refer to pharmaceutical or biochemical manufacturing and must be supported by the corresponding production license.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After a formal name-pre-approval rejection, the applicant must obtain the written reasons from the local Administration for Market Regulation. Within 15 working days, a supplementary corrective application with revised Chinese name components may be filed through the same name self-service declaration portal. If substantive refusal persists, the applicant may submit a written administrative reconsideration application to the municipal-level Administration for Market Regulation or the designated people's government within 60 days from the date of notification, attaching the rejection notice, proof of eligibility for the requested name, the legal basis for any sensitive token use, and a proposed alternative name. If administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, first-instance administrative litigation may be commenced before the relevant people's court within six months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 3250 pharmaceutical extraction WFOE, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable. The local Administration for Market Regulation and the provincial Medical Products Administration require an actual, purpose-built registered business premises capable of accommodating pharmaceutical-grade extraction, GMP workflows, controlled storage, environmental controls, and sanitation infrastructure. The municipal tax authority also rejects virtual addresses because invoice issuance, payroll reporting, VAT assessment, and corporate income tax filings require a verifiable physical establishment. A registered physical lease of at least two to three years and facility-fit documentation must be produced at incorporation and at the pharmaceutical license application stage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood, estimated at approximately 85 percent within the first operating year. Checklist: (1) unannounced SAMR address verification; (2) municipal tax bureau premises check on invoice and payroll records; (3) provincial medical products administration GMP inspection; (4) customs, safety, environmental, and fire authority inspections; (5) verification of employee presence, equipment installation, utility consumption, and production records. Any mismatch between the registered address, commercial substance, and physical operations may result in revocation of the business license, denial of tax-favourable status, and administrative penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), particularly Articles 4, 8, 23-27, 47-50, 52, 81-84, 90, 97 and 98; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 1-7, 12 and 15; Interim Measures for Market Subject Registration Management (2022); Measures for the Registration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises; and the State Administration for Market Regulation guidelines on electronic registration of enterprise establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration where the registered office is located, via the Unified Enterprise Registration Online System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and SAMR e-registration portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company (Enterprise Legal Person Business License Application) together with the Articles of Association and the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The PRC Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law impose no statutory minimum registered capital for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise engaged in pharmaceutical active ingredient manufacturing. China applies a subscribed capital regime. Nevertheless, for the ISIC 3250 heparin sodium anticoagulant manufacturing project, the registered capital must be commensurate with the production scale, expected fixed-asset investment, and GMP licensing requirements. A paid-in capital of no less than RMB 5,000,000, or the USD equivalent remitted into the company's designated foreign-currency capital account, is the recommended threshold to support drug manufacturing licensing, environmental approval and customs export registration. No government escrow or blocked capital account is required; funds are remitted directly into the company's own capital contribution account after the business license is issued and must be verified by a certified public accountant under the foreign exchange custody rules of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD (BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS)

WHEREAS, the Company is to be incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, with registered capital subscribed by the Hong Kong parent company, HK Investor [●];

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Board of Directors of CN_WFOE_LTD, acting in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Foreign Investment Law, as follows:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The registered capital of the Company shall be USD [●], divided into [●] registered capital contribution units. The sole shareholder hereby subscribes to all such units at par value and agrees to contribute such subscription, whether in lawful currency or in-kind pharmaceutical processing equipment and technical know-how, in accordance with the capital contribution schedule set out in Article [●] of the Articles of Association. The Board instructs the Chief Financial Officer to open a dedicated capital contribution bank account at a licensed commercial bank in the People's Republic of China, to receive all capital deposits, and to cause a certified public accountant to issue a capital contribution verification report after each contribution.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board adopts [●] Bank, [●] Branch, as the Company's principal banker. The Board authorizes the Legal Representative, the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer, any two acting jointly, to execute all account opening forms, loan documents, guarantee instruments, foreign exchange transactions, L/C and SWIFT payment instruments, and banking mandates on behalf of the Company. Any transaction exceeding RMB [●] shall require prior board approval. The banking records shall be preserved in the Company's corporate books.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [●], [●] District, [●] City, People's Republic of China, as set out in the Articles of Association. The Legal Representative is directed to file such address with the State Administration for Market Regulation and to register the same with the tax, customs, and statistics authorities.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [●] as Chairman and Legal Representative, [●] as General Manager, [●] as Chief Financial Officer, and [●] as Supervisor. Each officer shall hold office for a term of three years, renewable by subsequent board resolution. The Legal Representative shall exclusively represent the Company in dealings with all governmental agencies. The General Manager shall have full operational authority for the heparin sodium anticoagulant manufacturing project. The Supervisor shall independently monitor legal compliance, corporate finance, and statutory filing obligations.

5. Delegation and Authorization. The Board delegates to the above officers all necessary powers to prepare, execute, file, notarize and perfect the Company's business license registration, tax registration, social insurance registration, foreign exchange registration, Customs registration, drug manufacturing license, GMP certification, environmental impact assessment approval, Civil Defense fire clearance, and all ancillary industrial permits. The officers are hereby empowered to engage external counsel, notaries, certified public accountants, environmental consultants and licensing agents as required. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until superseded by a subsequent board resolution.

Unanimously approved by the Board of Directors on the date set forth above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Eligibility Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Unified Enterprise Registration Online System, local Municipal Market Supervision Administration e-window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the provincial Market Supervision Administration enterprise registration portal and enter the proposed English and Chinese company name, CN_WFOE_LTD, together with the intended business scope. Include a precise operating description covering 'manufacture, processing, fractionation and sale of heparin sodium anticoagulant, low-molecular-weight heparin, and related pharmaceutical active pharmaceutical ingredients' so that the registry can classify the company under permitted foreign investment activities. The platform will run an automatic conflict and prohibited-words check against the national name database and the Foreign Investment Access Negative List. Submit the name reservation application, choose limited liability company type, enter the proposed registered capital, proposed address, and legal representative details, then download the automatic name reservation notice. The notice is valid for six months and must be appended to the ultimate establishment application. If the negative list restricts or prohibits the pharmaceutical scope, the system will block submission, and the applicant must narrow the business scope or apply for a separate feasibility approval.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and business registration certificate of the Hong Kong parent company
Hong Kong parent company's certificate of good standing
Notarized and legalized corporate resolution of the Hong Kong investor authorizing WFOE incorporation
Passport copy of the appointed chairman / legal representative
Proposed company name confirmation form
Power of attorney appointing a PRC incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, conflict or prohibited wording, immediately submit a new name reservation number with a distinguishing trademark registration certificate. If the business scope triggers a foreign investment negative list restriction, revise the scope to a permitted downstream sales and distribution function and file a holding structure, or apply for a special approval from the National Development and Reform Commission and the local commerce authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Legalization and Authentication of the Hong Kong Investor Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China in Hong Kong, or a China-Appointed Attesting Officer in Hong Kong, followed by SAMR authentication acceptance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Hong Kong parent company dossier, including its certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, business registration certificate and board resolution authorizing the establishment of the WFOE. Arrange for a Hong Kong notary public or China-appointed attesting officer to certify that all copies are true duplicates of the originals. Thereafter, submit the certified copies to the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hong Kong for legalization. Once legalized, the entire document package must be translated into English and attached to the later SAMR registration filing. The legalization stamps and notary seals are mandatory because SAMR will conduct a chain-of-title and source-of-funds verification. If any document is incomplete, the notary must issue a supplementary certificate and the package must be re-authenticated. This step is critical to prove the non-resident investor's valid existence and the authority of the signatories.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of the Hong Kong investor
Notarized business registration certificate of the Hong Kong investor
Certificate of good standing issued within the last six months
Board resolution of Hong Kong investor approving the WFOE capital subscription
Notarized Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Association of Hong Kong investor
Passport of the principal director of the Hong Kong investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR deems the notarization non-compliant, return the package to the Hong Kong notary for fresh certification and repeat the legalization procedure. If legalization is delayed by the consular office, file a time-limited supplementary materials request with SAMR and provide an undertaking that the certified package will be delivered within ten additional business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Establishment Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (under SAMR) - online registration portal or administrative service hall physical window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard enterprise establishment registration application form on the unified SAMR online platform. Attach the name reservation notice, the authenticated Hong Kong investor documents, the Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder, the power of attorney, the registered office lease proof, and the written consent of the proposed legal representative, supervisor and directors. State the registered capital amount, the paid-in contribution schedule, and the legal representative name. Confirm that the board resolution and corporate governance provisions comply with the Company Law. Once submitted, the SAMR review officer performs a formal and substantive compliance review, including money-laundering screening of the Hong Kong investor beneficial owners. After approval, the electronic business license is generated and the company obtains legal personality. No official filing fee is payable. Print the electronic business license, apply for the electronic social credit code, and proceed to seal carving, tax registration and bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise establishment registration application form
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Name reservation notice from Step 1
Notarized and legalized Hong Kong investor documents from Step 2
Registered office proof (lease agreement with property ownership certificate copy)
Legal representative identity document and passport copy
Supervisor identity document and passport copy
Power of attorney and agent identity card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a notice to supplement or rectify documents, respond within the statutory fifteen-day correction period through the online portal. If the application is rejected on substantive grounds, amend the Articles of Association and re-submit a fresh application, then file administrative reconsideration with the next-level SAMR if the rejection is arbitrary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Seal Carving, Tax Registration, Social Insurance and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau designated seal engraving enterprises, State Taxation Administration e-tax system, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security service centres, and a licensed PRC commercial bank with foreign exchange business authorization, with State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) registration completed through the bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, obtain the enterprise social credit code and apply to the public security bureau approved seal carver for the official company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative personal seal. Register the company with the State Taxation Administration through the local e-tax platform, elect a tax collection district, select general taxpayer status if projected annual turnover exceeds the regulatory threshold, and apply for invoice issuance. Open a basic deposit RMB bank account and a foreign-currency capital account at the chosen commercial bank, and remit any required initial paid-in capital. Furnish the bank with the business license, the board resolution appointing bankers and authorized signatories, a beneficial ownership declaration, and the company's corporate charter. The bank will complete SAFE foreign exchange registration for the foreign investor's capital account. Thereafter, register for social insurance, housing fund and work-related injury insurance at the local government service centre, and complete any required record-filing for employment contracts.
required_dossiers: Business license electronic printout
Legal representative identity document and passport
Board resolution appointing banker and authorized signatories
Beneficial ownership declaration and corporate ownership chart
Articles of Association
Seal registration application with police approval
Tax registration information form
Social insurance registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to the medium-risk pharmaceutical manufacturing classification, provide a further board resolution, beneficial ownership declaration and project narrative, and escalate the file to the bank's compliance officer. If tax registration is delayed, use the integrated one-stop window of the local market supervision administration and present the social credit code and lease contract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance Ratification, Capital Contribution Completion and Statutory Books Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's Board of Directors and sole shareholder, with a PRC certified public accountant for capital verification and SAMR enterprise annual reporting system for any paid-in capital record filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first formal board meeting, or obtain a unanimous written consent resolution, to ratify all pre-registration actions, approve the internal financial and treasury regulations, adopt labour and payroll rules, and designate authorized signatories for contracts, permits and regulatory filings. Execute the capital contribution subscription letter and cause the Hong Kong investor to remit the approved paid-in capital to the dedicated capital contribution bank account in compliance with SAFE rules. Engage a licensed PRC certified public accountant to verify the contribution and issue a capital verification report. Record shareholder details, director appointments, supervisor appointment and capital contribution history in the statutory register of members. File any paid-in capital change with SAMR through the enterprise information disclosure system, and maintain complete statutory books, meeting minutes, resolutions, share transfer records and accounting ledgers at the registered office. This step closes the governance loop and prepares the company to apply for drug manufacturing and environmental permits.
required_dossiers: First board resolution ratification package
Sole shareholder written decision and subscription letter
Bank capital contribution deposit certificate
SAFE foreign exchange contribution bank filing
Certified public accountant capital verification report
Statutory register of shareholders
Director and supervisor appointment letters
Internal governance and financial policies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Hong Kong investor fails to remit capital before the agreed date, cause the board to pass a supplemental resolution amending the contribution schedule, apply for a SAFE extension, and record the new schedule in the Articles of Association through a change filing. If the CPA refuses to issue a verification report, resolve the underlying remittance discrepancy by returning excess amounts or correcting the capital account and bank documentary records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) through the provincial drug administration; local Emergency Management Bureau for workplace safety; local Fire and Rescue Bureau for Civil Defense fire safety; and the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration for pharmaceutical production licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing License (Drug Production License) and Drug GMP Certificate (Good Manufacturing Practice Certification), supplemented by a Hazardous Chemical Business Permit if organic solvents are stored in bulk quantities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the provincial Ecology and Environment Department.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class I construction project requiring a full Environmental Impact Report (EIA Report) with public participation and approval by the provincial Ecology and Environment Department. The project is classified as a pharmaceutical chemical processing facility because heparin sodium extraction and low-molecular-weight heparin fractionation involve organic solvents, acidic/alkaline process effluents, activated resin regeneration and spent solvent recovery.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must meet GB 21903-2008 'Discharge Standard of Water Pollutants for Pharmaceutical Industry' and GB 8978-1996 Class III limits: chemical oxygen demand (COD) 100 mg/L maximum, five-day biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) 30 mg/L maximum, suspended solids (SS) 70 mg/L maximum, ammonia nitrogen 15 mg/L maximum, total phosphorus 0.5 mg/L maximum, pH 6 to 9. Atmospheric volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from fractionation, solvent recovery and cleanroom exhaust must not exceed 80 mg/m3, with a solvent recovery or catalytic oxidation system achieving at least 90% removal efficiency. Hazardous waste, including spent organic solvents, activated carbon, filter cakes and contaminated laboratory materials, must be segregated, stored in a licensed waste depot, manifested and disposed only through a company holding a hazardous waste business license.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain a Fire Protection Acceptance Certificate from the municipal Fire and Rescue Bureau verifying installation and functionality of fire suppression systems, flammable solvent storage compliance, smoke detection and alarm systems, emergency exits, and pressurization of clean-rooms. A structural load inspection certificate must be issued by a qualified engineering institute, confirming floor design loads for the fractionation columns, solvent tanks and autoclave equipment meet national building code requirements. Occupational health and safety clearance must be obtained from the local Emergency Management Bureau under the Work Safety Law, covering process hazard analysis, hazardous chemical registration, explosion-proof electrical classification, personal protective equipment programs, and an emergency response plan. Additionally, pressure vessels and sterilization boilers must be registered with the SAMR special equipment supervision authority before use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating through provincial and county-level competent tax offices; online taxpayer portal is the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) platform and the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE is a Chinese resident legal person, so the statutory TIN/VAT ID is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation upon business license registration. The foreign non-resident shareholder does not obtain the WFOE TIN; the WFOE itself completes tax information registration within 30 days after receiving the business license through the competent STA office or the Electronic Tax Bureau. Required filings include the business license, articles of association, legal representative identification, shareholder identification, bank account details, registered office proof, and entity formation documents. The STA then activates the taxpayer profile for Corporate Income Tax, Value Added Tax, stamp duty, and withholding obligations. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment is separately registered by the WFOE as withholding agent when dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees are remitted, and a withholding taxpayer code is created at that time.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income at the standard 25% Corporate Income Tax rate; no pass-through or territorial exemption is available for the WFOE's operating income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under PRC tax law. The WFOE may elect between small-scale VAT taxpayer status and general VAT taxpayer status below the RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales threshold, but general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory above that threshold and is the necessary election to access export zero-rating and input VAT refund.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: China Value Added Tax (VAT), administered by the State Taxation Administration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All WFOEs must complete tax registration at formation regardless of turnover; mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. Export-oriented WFOEs may voluntarily register as general VAT taxpayers below the threshold to obtain input VAT credits and export refund eligibility.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates fully digitalized electronic invoices (FDEI) issued through STA-approved channels, with real-time fiscal clearance via the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform integrated with Golden Tax Phase IV. VAT invoices must carry standardized commodity tax classification codes, unique invoice identifiers, digital encryption, and be transmitted electronically to the STA through prescribed API/data exchange interfaces. For export transactions, invoice data is matched with customs declarations and foreign exchange collection records through the China International Trade Single Window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A general VAT taxpayer WFOE may claim 0% VAT on the export supply of heparin sodium anticoagulant only if the goods are physically exported outside PRC customs territory, covered by a valid Customs export declaration, sold to an overseas buyer under a genuine export contract, supported by a Special VAT invoice for export, and the foreign currency sales proceeds are received and repatriated into China within the statutory 180-day deadline. The corresponding input VAT embedded in the exported goods may then be recovered through the export tax rebate (export drawback) procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document such as air waybill
Commercial invoice and signed export contract
Bank receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency evidencing inward remittance and repatriation into China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are scrutinized by STA and PRC Customs via matched data from the China International Trade Single Window, including customs declarations, electronic invoices, logistics transport records, and bank foreign exchange receipts. If a claim is unverified, fraudulent, or the export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline, the STA disallows the zero-rating, claws back any VAT refunded, imposes daily late-payment surcharges at 0.05%, and may assess administrative penalties of one to five times the amount of the fraudulently obtained refund under the Law of the PRC on the Administration of Tax Collection. Serious cases are referred for criminal prosecution for fraudulent export tax refund, and the exporter may be downgraded or removed from export tax rebate eligibility with retrospective reassessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the foreign-exchange administrator sitting under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates an administered float with current-account convertibility achieved under the 1996 IMF Article VIII obligation, but capital-account items remain subject to comprehensive approval and registration. A mainland WFOE's equity capital injected from Hong Kong is treated as foreign direct investment and can be converted into RMB only through a designated foreign exchange capital account after SAFE registration. Routine current-account payments such as import settlement, royalties and profit remittance are permitted without pre-approval if a valid transaction document and a genuine underlying trade or service are presented, but banks must perform a genuineness and compliance review. Profit remittances to the Hong Kong shareholder are not freely automatic: the WFOE must provide certified audited financial statements, Chinese tax clearance certificates including withholding income tax on dividends, board resolutions on dividend distribution, and a bank verification on the fund-generating position. Surrender rules for export proceeds have been liberalised; mandatory conversion at a fixed ratio no longer applies, but all export foreign currency must be received into a domestic foreign exchange account, registered in the trade monitoring system, and either retained or settled within the permitted framework. The absence of full capital-account opening means cross-border financing, guarantee and derivative activities require registration or prior approval, and any attempt to access offshore hedging markets is restricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the PRC Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring scheme, export proceeds must be repatriated and credited to the exporter's foreign exchange settlement account within the banking system; the exporter has a maximum of five working days after receipt to automatically match the proceeds against outstanding Customs export declarations in the monitoring system, and may then choose voluntary settlement into RMB or retention. There is no fixed compulsory conversion percentage. For exporters classified under Category B or C due to prior violations, SAFE may impose stricter settlement verification and documentary review for each transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Capital Account for FDI capital escrow and separate RMB Basic Deposit Account for operational settlement

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account with dual-currency trade settlement sub-ledger for export proceeds and import disbursements
Capital verification / escrow account for inbound HK equity injection and temporary RMB settlement account before SAFE registration is completed

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (for example Revolut Business or Wise Multi-Currency) cannot serve as the primary banking or clearing account for a mainland China WFOE. Legal constraints restrict onshore RMB settlement and SAFE-registered foreign exchange transactions to licensed Chinese banks; EMIs without a PBOC or SAFE licence have no access to CIPS or CNY clearing, and are prohibited from holding enterprise funds under the Administrative Measures for E-commerce Payment. The only marginal role is as an auxiliary collection wallet for non-mainland customer receipts routed later to the onshore bank, but this does not replace the statutory accounts. Feasibility rating is Low; legally non-viable as a principal treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative of the WFOE, or a senior authorised officer holding a written board authorisation, must appear physically at the PRC bank branch for face-to-face interview and original document verification. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a basic RMB deposit account because the PBOC account settlement provisions require bank staff to verify identity and intent directly. Some banks permit a video pre-verification, but final signing and seal-filing require the presence of an authorised signatory at the branch. The Hong Kong parent directors can participate remotely, but cannot substitute the WFOE's physical appearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner and source-of-wealth opacity: HK holding company injects equity but the bank cannot verify personal wealth of the non-resident founders behind the Hong Kong vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Hong Kong business registration, Annual Return and CRS/UBO register; complete corporate ownership chain to natural persons; founders' passport copies and proof of address; two bank reference letters; HK audited financial statements for the past two years; statutory source-of-wealth declaration; and a group structure chart signed by all directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical chemical inputs imported from non-EU and non-US jurisdictions trigger trade-based money laundering and sanctions red flags, especially bill-of-lading mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, packing lists, underlying supply contracts, original bills of lading or airway bills, PRC Customs export declarations, GMP/ISO quality certificates, import quarantine certificates for raw material, supplier export licence and ISO certificates, plus a trade-margin analysis proving prices are within the Customs price reference band.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Irregular dividend or profit remittance history from the Hong Kong parent creates tax evasion and round-tripping suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chinese tax e-filing acknowledgements, Certified Chinese auditor's report for the WFOE, bank foreign-exchange settlement records, board resolutions declaring dividends, withholding tax settlement receipts for remitted amounts, and a HK tax representative letter confirming the dividend source is not undeclared mainland operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No verifiable physical manufacturing footprint: virtual company suspicion for the active pharmaceutical ingredient extraction business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Factory lease agreement, geo-tagged site photos, production floor equipment list, ISO 13485 or ISO 9001 certificate, drug manufacturing licence (GMP analogue), onshore utility invoices for water and power, payroll records for onshore chemists, and the Environmental Protection Bureau production permit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital from the HK parent must be routed via SWIFT MT103 into the designated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a SAFE-registered bank branch. The remitter must use the balance-of-payments purpose code 622011 for capital contribution to a foreign-invested enterprise and clearly disclose the remitter and beneficiary relationship. The WFOE must present the SAFE FDI establishment and change registration record, the bank account permit, and the overseas director board resolution authorising the transfer. After credit, the bank validates the transaction genuineness; RMB conversion is permitted only against a compliant capital payment intention and cannot be transferred to a non-operating account. Although a statutory capital verification report is no longer always required, the bank issues a deposit confirmation that the company can use for tax and accounting records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of imported raw materials, freight and export support services is executed through (a) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for frequent or smaller payments with the underlying contract and Customs declaration pre-scanned through the bank single-window portal, (b) irrevocable documentary letters of credit opened by the WFOE bank for larger consignments, and (c) documentary collections with collection on presentation of documents given moderate counterparty trust. Every disbursement must be linked to a real foreign-exchange purchase and a payment application form under the PRC current-account trade regime; the bank checks sanctions screening, invoice-to-Customs value alignment and the beneficiary name match.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB/foreign-exchange forward contracts quoted by a licensed SAFE bank for matched trade cash-flow dates, subject to the real-demand principle and existing underlying trade exposure.
RMB/foreign-exchange currency swaps for rolling short-term liquidity conversion between CNY and USD or HKD for current-account transactions.
Zero-cost collar structures combining bought and sold FX options for hedging USD or EUR trade receivables, with the bank verifying the underlying transaction size and tenor.

Onshore deliverable FX options include call spreads and barrier options linked to genuine export or import cash flows, while noting that non-deliverable forwards and offshore NDF contracts are not permissible for mainland entities under SAFE real-demand rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Government of the Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after every anniversary of incorporation. For example, a company incorporated on 15 March must deliver the annual return on or before 26 April each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs escalating penalties of HK$1,200 if delivered within 3 months after the 42-day deadline, HK$2,400 for 3-6 months, HK$3,600 for 6-9 months, and HK$4,800 for more than 9 months. On prosecution, directors and officers may be fined up to HK$50,000 plus a daily default fine of HK$1,000. Continual non-delivery may trigger gazetted administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal (one-year or three-year certificate payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department / Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the expiry date of the current Business Registration Certificate; a one-month grace period exists upon payment of a HK$300 late fee.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a HK$300 surcharge. Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence carrying a fine of up to HK$5,000 and imprisonment for up to one year. Continued non-renewal also enables IRD enforcement and can support Companies Registry strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) filed together with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department / Profits Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date of issue of BIR51. For a 31 December accounting period, the return is ordinarily issued in April and the base deadline is 1 May, subject to approved tax representative block extension rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in an estimated assessment, automatic penalty of HK$10,000, and interest. Knowingly furnishing an incorrect return is punishable by a HK$50,000 penalty plus additional tax up to three times the amount undercharged. Willful evasion may lead to criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and BIR56B) including nil returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department / Employer's Return Processing Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date of BIR56A. For the year of assessment ended 31 March, the return is typically issued in April and due no later than 1 May, or the date stated on the form.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence with an automatic penalty of HK$10,000. Incorrect returns furnished without reasonable excuse attract a HK$50,000 penalty and additional tax up to three times the undercharged amount. Directors and responsible officers may also be prosecuted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register (SCR) annual internal review and continuous update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with an external authority; maintained at the registered office or a prescribed place in Hong Kong for on-demand inspection by the Companies Registry and law enforcement agencies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuing obligation throughout the year. Registrable changes must be entered within 7 days of becoming known to the company; a formal review should be performed at least once each financial year and no later than the date of signing the annual financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep an accurate and current SCR is an offence. On summary conviction the company and every responsible officer may be fined up to HK$50,000, with a further daily default fine of HK$1,000. Persistent non-compliance can also trigger regulatory investigations and strike-off risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In Hong Kong, every company incorporated under the Companies Ordinance must undergo an annual statutory audit by an independent certified public accountant unless it is dormant or classifies as a small private company or small guarantee company and validly waives the audit requirement. A company loses audit exemption if it exceeds at least two of the following quantitative thresholds in a financial year: annual revenue above HK$20 million; total assets above HK$10 million; or more than 50 employees. The exemption is unavailable to banks, insurance companies, licensed corporations under the Securities and Futures Ordinance, and any company that is a member of a group required to prepare consolidated financial statements. A member holding 5% or more of the voting rights may also veto the waiver. Therefore a non-ex

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 25% rate may be reduced to 15% for High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) status under Article 28 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law; R&D expenses enjoy an additional 100% super-deduction on qualifying expenditures (200% overall deduction); technology transfer income is partially exempt; preferential 15% rate may apply in encouraged Western regions and certain Free Trade Zone schemes; no patent box regime applies to heparin sodium manufacturing as currently enacted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China for General Enterprises) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-tax channel
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 5 months after the end of the tax year (on or before May 31 of the following year). Quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after each quarter end, using Form A200000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue: gross sales revenue from the sale of heparin sodium API, processed anticoagulant goods and related freight, excluding VAT, after sales returns and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all export sales to the Hong Kong related party at arm's length prices. Retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for any sales to the Hong Kong buyer. Complete Schedule A105010 (Related Party Transactions) and attach a transfer pricing disclosure form if aggregate related-party transaction thresholds are met. No dividend or royalty withholding arises on revenue recognition itself, but the enterprise must separately declare any non-resident payments embedded in the transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs and expenses: direct cost of crude heparin raw materials, reagents, manufacturing labor, manufacturing overhead and production depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For purchases from the Hong Kong related party, ensure prices reflect the arm's length standard; misstatements here may trigger CIT adjustments for understatement of taxable profits. Imported materials from Hong Kong must be declared with customs and import VAT; the invoice set must be genuine. False procurement invoices are a criminal red flag and are adjusted entirely off the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses: general office costs, professional fees, statutory licensing fees, pharmaceutical certification costs, and deductible technical royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to the Hong Kong parent for the use of know-how or patents are deductible only when the intangible is actually used in China and the amount is arm's length and supported by a cost-sharing or license agreement. When making the royalty payment, withhold income tax at 10% (statutory) and apply for the Hong Kong DTA-5% treaty rate using the tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership self-assessment. The deduction must be reduced if the withhold tax is not actually remitted to the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: interest expense and bank fees on intercompany borrowings, letter-of-credit charges and foreign exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a Hong Kong shareholder is subject to thin capitalisation limitation (debt-to-equity ratio 2:1 for non-financial enterprises). Interest that exceeds the statutory ratio is non-deductible. Outbound interest payments carry 10% statutory WHT, reduced to 7% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement when the beneficial owner is the Hong Kong lender and holds a valid tax residency certificate. Failing to withhold on interest paid to Hong Kong will lead to a tax charge plus a penalty under the Tax Collection and Administration Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit: the net profit or loss after deducting all business expenses from revenue, before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line is the foundation for all tax adjustments. Profit must be computed in accordance with Chinas Accounting Standards; any cross-border non-arms-length under-pricing of outbound heparin API sales or over-pricing of inbound logistics services from Hong Kong will distort this figure and must be adjusted. Directors are required to ensure the recorded profit is the real economic profit of the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: the tax base after add-backs and deductions, including prior-year loss carry-forward, tax-exempt income and other timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule A105000 for reconciling differences. Deductible foreign tax credits must be evidenced on Schedule A108030. The loss carry-forward limit is 5 years for ordinary enterprises and 10 years for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises. If the Hong Kong parent is a shell and the treaty benefit has been denied, the WFOE may also need to increase taxable income by the amount of WHT not borne as a contractual adjustment; all such items should be reflected in this reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate and income tax payable: the headline 25% rate or 15% HNTE rate applied to taxable income to derive the expected annual tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When using the reduced 15% HNTE rate, attach a copy of the valid HNTE certificate and submit Schedule A107041. If the WFOE loses its HNTE status, the benefit is retroactively withdrawn with interest. The ultimate Hong Kong shareholder has no direct taxing right at the entity level; the WFOE is the taxpayer for Chinese corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net balance of tax payable / refund receivable: annual tax payable less quarterly prepayments, tax credits and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the annual tax payable exceeds prepayments, balance must be settled by the statutory deadline. If a refund arises from the foreign tax credit or loss carry-back, apply for the refund through the e-tax board. Distributions of after-tax profits to the Hong Kong parent must first satisfy this final tax position, then be reduced by the applicable dividend withholding tax at the time the board declares and approves the dividend.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: statutory fine of RMB 2,000 (up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases) plus a daily surcharge of 0.05% on overdue tax. Deliberate under-declaration of income or inflated deductions triggers a penalty of 50% up to 3 times the unpaid tax, plus daily interest surcharges. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 carries imprisonment of up to 7 years and a criminal fine where the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of taxable income; fraudulent VAT invoicing may be prosecuted under Criminal Law Article 205 with exposure up to life imprisonment for exceptional magnitude.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (statutory rate on dividends distributed by a PRC resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, imposed under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 3 and Article 37)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced 5% Mainland-Hong Kong DTA rate (applicable when the Hong Kong shareholder holds at least 25% of the WFOE's equity), the withholding agent (WFOE) must obtain the following prior to distribution: (i) a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong, ordinarily covering the year of distribution; (ii) a beneficial ownership self-assessment completed by the Hong Kong parent, proving the Hong Kong entity has the right to possession and control of the dividend, with substantive business activity in Hong Kong; (iii) a PRC treaty relief declaration form (e.g., Form F220) and supporting documents submitted to the State Taxation Administration local office, either through the withholding declaration process or via a 'non-resident enjoy treaty treatment' filing on the e-tax portal. The WFOE as withholding agent must obtain each document, keep it in the file with the annual return, and withhold at the treaty rate only after the relevant filing is accepted. The 5% rate is unavailable to a shell Hong Kong company lacking core income-generating activities; the statutory 10% rate must then be withheld. Dividends paid in non-cash form or as non-monetary distributions attract the same WHT and DTA mechanics.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: PRC statutory WHT on interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10%; under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement the treaty rate is 7% of the gross interest. Royalties: PRC statutory WHT on royalties is 10%; under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement, the rate is reduced to 5% for royalties generated by industrial know-how, patents and technical assistance in the science field (including pharmaceutical extraction processes). Both treaty rates require a Hong Kong TRC and evidence of beneficial ownership. In the absence of treaty protection, additional VAT on royalties (6% or 13% depending on the service character) and urban/maintenance taxes may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File preparation is triggered when: (i) related-party tangible asset transfers exceed RMB 200 million; (ii) related-party intangible asset or financial asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million; or (iii) related-party provision of services exceeds RMB 40 million; the same RMB 40 million threshold applies to interest and loans with related parties. A Master File is required for an enterprise whose group has consolidated annual revenue exceeding RMB 5 billion and whose Chinese related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million. An enterprise may also be required, upon SAT notice, to prepare a benchmarking study or other country-by-country report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulation to resident WFOEs because the WFOE is already taxed on its substantive production. However, economic substance is decisive for the Hong Kong parent when invoking the DTA relief and for the entire group under the PRC General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, implemented by SAT Circular 6/2016 and Circular 5/2017). The Hong Kong entity claiming treaty benefits must perform the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Hong Kong, meaning it must have an actual office, employees, board direction and transaction decision-making in Hong Kong. If the Hong Kong parent is an empty shell, the dividend, interest and royalty income will be re-characterised by the Chinese tax authority as taxable to the substantial mainland beneficiary and treaty relief will be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE systematically sells heparin sodium API to its Hong Kong related party at a price below the arm's length wholesale price (e.g., a 40% discount) without an economically justifiable reason, thereby understating mainland taxable income. The WFOE also fails to prepare contemporaneous documentation for the related-party export sales in excess of the local file threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41 empowers the tax authority to re-assess the transaction; Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 imposes a fine of 50% to 3 times the unpaid tax plus daily overdue surcharge. Criminal Law Article 201 applies where the under-reported tax amount is significant, leading to criminal fines and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise the mispricing can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall through the Law of Tort or the Company Law Article 20 principle. They may be placed on the 'non-normal exit control' travel ban by the exit-entry administration, have personal assets frozen or confiscated, and risk criminal detention; in particularly severe cases a criminal court can sentence the responsible officer to imprisonment under Article 201.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is an offshore shell with no Hong Kong employees, office, bank account or substantive management, yet the WFOE withholds only the reduced 5% Mainland-Hong Kong DTA rate on a dividend distribution, rather than the 10% statutory rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under STA Public Notice 2015/60 and the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement general anti-abuse clauses, the treaty right is denied; the tax authority re-characterises the dividend as subject to 10% withholding, plus penalty under Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 (50%-3 times) and daily surcharge. The enterprise may also be blacklisted for tax credit violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of both the WFOE and the Hong Kong shell risk personal enforcement: they can be made civilly liable for the unpaid withholding and penalties, be prohibited from leaving mainland China (exit control / travel ban), lose personal assets through property seizure, and be criminally prosecuted for tax evasion where the under-withheld amount is large and the conduct is deliberate. The director who signed the dividend declaration and the WHT return bears the primary criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE generates fraudulent VAT special invoices from shell suppliers to inflate raw material costs of heparin production (e.g., fake invoices for annual procurement of unrealistically high volumes of pig intestinal mucosa), thereby evading both VAT and corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Article 205 punishes the issuance, use or creation of false VAT special invoices with a fine of 2 to 20 times the false amount and imprisonment up to 7 years for standard occurrences; aggravated cases can lead to life imprisonment. Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 additionally assesses the evaded tax with a 50%-5 times penalty. The false invoices are entirely non-deductible for CIT and disallow the input VAT credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and CFO who signed or knowingly relied on the fictitious invoices face criminal arrest, asset confiscation, and a personal travel ban on leaving China. On a conviction, they may be sentenced to a prison term; they are also barred from acting as a director or honorary manager in China (director disqualification), and the civil court will order restitution of corporate losses directly out of their personal bank accounts and shareholdings.
